fullPassage:
[1번] One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps process sensory information. When it is damaged, patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only shave the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only apply it to the right side of her face.

[2번] Many people are embarrassed by the sound of their own voice. It doesn't bother them when they are having a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it. There is actually a scientific explanation for this. We usually hear our own voice while talking to other people, and when we do so, we receive the sound in two different ways. It arrives externally through the air, just like the sound of other people's voices. But it also arrives internally, because it moves through the bones of our skull. On the other hand, when we hear a recording of our voice, the sound only travels through the air. Sound that travels through bone is perceived as being deeper than sound that travels through the air. So we often find that our voice has a higher pitch than what we expected when we hear it on a recording. Our voice is an important part of our identity. Therefore, it is a little upsetting to find out it doesn't sound like what we thought!

[3번] Light is a mixture of all the colors of the rainbow. Different wavelengths of light are different colors. Blue wavelengths — which help us during the day by improving our mood and increasing our attention span — seem to be the most disruptive at night. Device screens, along with energy-efficient lighting, are increasing the amount of blue wavelengths we are regularly exposed to after sunset. Studies suggest that blue light affects our production of melatonin, a hormone that helps us sleep, more than other types of light. It suppresses melatonin production and damages our sleep patterns. In an experiment, Canadian researchers compared the melatonin levels of two groups of people. One group wore special goggles that blocked blue light while exposed to bright light. The other did not wear goggles and was exposed to regular light. The fact that the melatonin levels of the group without goggles were the same as those of the first group supports the theory that blue light is harming our sleep.

[4번] Brazil's Jungle Marathon, held in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions. There are three races — a 42-kilometer marathon, a 127-kilometer four-stage race, and a 254-kilometer six-stage race — that participants can choose from. The six-stage race is clearly the most difficult, taking participants more than a week to complete. The races all go through swamps, across rivers, and along beaches. Only basic necessities such as shelter, first aid, and drinking water are provided, so the runners have to carry their own food and survival equipment. Despite its difficulties and dangers, the event attracts athletes from around the world who can't resist the opportunity to compete in a beautiful natural environment.

[5번] Surprisingly, the English word "alcohol" originally referred to a kind of eyeshadow. In Ancient Egypt, the mineral stibnite was heated to put it through sublimation, the process of turning a solid into a gas. The smoky vapor that was produced left a layer of black powder that could be collected. They used the powder to produce a thick paste, which was then used as eyeshadow. This paste was called kohl, an Arabic term meaning "stain" or "paint." This term was combined with al-, the Arabic word for "the", to create al-kohl, the Arabic word for eyeshadow made from sublimated stibnite. In the mid-1500s, chemists and alchemists discovered this term in ancient textbooks and had a realization that sublimation could draw the purest essence out of something. They began applying this process to liquids produced through a similar process of distillation. Over time, it led to liquors being simply known as "alcohol."

[6번] The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first proposed by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should assume that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can avoid being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely reject slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.

[7번] Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it unafraid of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great advantage when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 sharp teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.

[8번] In the Parana Delta near Buenos Aires, Argentina, is a small island called "The Eye," which floats in the middle of a small lake that is about 120 meters in diameter. It was accidentally discovered by Argentinian film director Sergio Neuspiller during the pre-production for a horror film about extraterrestrials. Interestingly, both the island and the lake are perfectly circular. What's more, the lake that surrounds the island is extremely cold and clear — an unusual phenomenon for the area. So mysterious is the island that people have wondered if it was created naturally or by aliens. Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents flowing to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's unusually cold, clear water.

questions.passage: One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is called "hemispatial neglect." This occurs when there is damage to the brain's parietal lobe, which helps process sensory information. When it is (A)[damaged / healed], patients cannot perceive people, sounds, and objects on one side of their body. Each of the brain's hemispheres controls the other side of the body, so patients cannot sense what is on the opposite side of the brain damage. For example, a man with damage to the left side of the brain cannot perceive what is on the right. As a result, he might only (B)[cover / shave] the left side of his face. Similarly, what if a woman suffering from damage to the right side of the brain put on makeup? She would only (C)[remove / apply] it to the right side of her face.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) damaged=손상된 / healed=치유된 (B) shave=면도하다 / cover=가리다 (C) apply=(화장품을) 바르다 / remove=지우다
det.analysis:
① healed—shave—remove: (A) 치유되면 인지를 잃지 않으므로 damaged가 맞음
② damaged—cover—remove: (B) 인지하는 왼쪽만 '면도'하는 것이지 가리는 게 아님
③ damaged—shave—apply: '손상'되면 인지 상실, 왼쪽만 '면도', 화장을 오른쪽에만 '바름' ←정답
④ healed—cover—apply: (A)(B) 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: '손상'(damaged)되면 인지 상실 → 인지되는 쪽만 '면도'(shave)/화장을 '바름'(apply)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 deeper와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: deeper=더 깊은 / shallower=더 얕은 / wider=더 넓은 / darker=더 어두운 / colder=더 차가운
det.analysis:

③ darker: 더 어두운 — 의미축 다름

questions.passage:

(B) After the long hike up the steep hill, she wanted only a <u>light</u> meal for dinner. She had a small bowl of soup and some salad instead of the heavy, oily food her friends ordered.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 light의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: light: (A) 빛 (B) (양이 적은) 가벼운
det.analysis:
① (A) 빛 (B) 가벼운: (A)는 화면에서 나오는 파란 '빛', (B)는 양이 적은 '가벼운' 식사 ←정답
② (A) 가벼운 (B) 빛: (A)를 '가벼운'으로 보면 화면에서 나오는 것과 안 맞음
③ (A) 빛 (B) 빛: (B)는 소량의 식사라 '빛'이 아니라 '가벼운'
④ (A) 가벼운 (B) 가벼운: (A)가 부적절
det.tip: light의 다의어: 화면에서 나오는 '빛' vs 양이 적은 '가벼운'

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) choose=선택하다 / escape=탈출하다 (B) complete=완주하다 / begin=시작하다 (C) beautiful=아름다운 / dangerous=위험한
det.analysis:
① escape/dangerous: 세 경주를 '탈출한다'? 아름다운 자연을 '위험한'으로? 문맥과 어긋남
② begin: 일주일 넘게 걸려 '시작한다'? '완주(complete)'해야 자연스러움
③ escape/dangerous: 모두 문맥과 반대
④ choose—complete—beautiful: 세 경주 중 '선택'하고, 완주(complete)에 일주일 넘게 걸리며, '아름다운' 자연에서 경쟁 ←정답
det.tip: 세 경주 중 선택(choose)하고, 완주(complete)에 오래 걸리며, 아름다운(beautiful) 자연

questions.passage:
(A) By heating the plant for hours, the scientists were able to <u>draw</u> the essential oils out of its leaves. The pure liquid was then stored in small glass bottles.

(B) The little girl liked to <u>draw</u> colorful pictures of her family with crayons. She proudly hung every one of them on the refrigerator door.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 draw의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: draw: (A) 이끌어 내다, 추출하다(동사) (B) 그림을 그리다(동사)
det.analysis:
① (A) 그리다 (B) 이끌어 내다: 의미가 뒤바뀌었어요.
② (A) 이끌어 내다, 추출하다 (B) 그리다: (A)는 잎에서 기름을 '뽑아냈다'는 뜻, (B)는 크레용으로 그림을 '그린다'는 뜻이에요 ←정답
③ (A) 그리다 (B) 그리다: (A)는 기름을 뽑아내는 것이라 '그리다'가 아니에요.
④ (A) 이끌어 내다 (B) 비기다: (B)는 그림을 그리는 것이라 '비기다'가 아니에요.
det.tip: draw의 다의어: 이끌어 내다/추출하다 vs 그림을 그리다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① proposed=제안된 ② assume→doubt (부적절) ③ reject=거부하다 ④ generous=관대한
det.analysis:
① proposed: 처음 제안된 개념 — 적절
② doubt: 어떤 위치든 될 수 있다고 '의심해야' 한다? 편견을 없애려면 '가정해야(assume)' 함이 원문 ←정답
③ reject: 노예제를 거부하다 — 적절
④ generous: 관대한 사회 복지 정책 — 적절
det.tip: 어떤 위치든 될 수 있다고 assume(가정). doubt(의심)는 흐름과 어긋남

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: warning=경고 / price=가격 / explanation=설명 / shadow=그림자
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞 'still no(여전히 ~없다)'와 뒤 '차갑고 맑은 물'이 단서예요.
① warning: 경고? 물의 원인을 밝히는 맥락과 무관
② price: 가격? 문맥 무관

④ shadow: 그림자? 문맥 무관
det.tip: still no ___ (여전히 밝혀지지 않음) → 설명(explanation)이 없음

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "to notice or become aware of something, especially through sight, hearing, or the other senses"

det.korean: ignore=무시하다 / perceive=인지하다 / invent=발명하다 / recall=기억해내다
det.analysis:

② perceive: 감각을 통해 무언가를 알아차리다·인지하다 ←정답
③ invent: 발명하다 — 인지와 무관
④ recall: 기억해내다 — 감각 인지와 다름
det.tip: 감각(시각·청각 등)을 통해 알아차리다 = perceive(인지하다)

① destroyed(파괴된): produced와 반대예요.
② hidden(숨겨진): 의미가 달라요.
③ delayed(미뤄진): 의미가 달라요.
④ made(만들어진): 증기가 '생겨났다/만들어졌다'는 점에서 produced의 동의어예요 ←정답
det.tip: produced(생겨난, 만들어진)와 가까운 것은 made(만들어진)

questions.passage: The "veil of ignorance" is a concept that was first ①<u>proposed</u> by the political philosopher John Rawls. The idea can be summed up as follows: When setting up laws for a society, you should ②<u>assume</u> that you could end up in any social position. By doing so, you can ③<u>avoid</u> being biased by your current situation. Following this way of thinking, people would likely ④<u>support</u> slavery because there is a chance that they could find themselves as slaves instead of slave owners. Rawls believed that by keeping the "veil of ignorance" in mind, society would naturally adopt fair, social-democratic policies. When you don't know where you will be on the socioeconomic ladder, strong redistribution and generous social welfare policies become much more attractive.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① proposed=제안된 ② assume=가정하다 ③ avoid=피하다 ④ reject→support (부적절)
det.analysis:
① proposed: Rawls가 처음 제안한 개념 — 적절
② assume: 어떤 위치든 될 수 있다고 가정하다 — 적절
③ avoid: 현재 상황에 편향되는 것을 피하다 — 적절
④ support: 사람들이 노예제를 '지지'한다? 자신이 노예가 될 수도 있으니 '거부한다(reject)'가 원문 ←정답
det.tip: 노예가 될 수도 있으니 노예제를 reject(거부). support(지지)는 흐름과 반대

questions.passage: Snakes are feared by humans and most animals. There is, however, one animal that does not fear them at all — the mongoose. Not only is it (A)[unafraid / afraid] of snakes, but it also hunts them as prey. The thick fur of the mongoose helps protect it from snake bites, and so does its quickness. It is capable of moving at speeds of more than 30 kph. This, along with its slender body, gives it a great (B)[advantage / weakness] when fighting snakes. Not only can it avoid the jaws of most snake species, but it can also survive when it does get bitten. Rare indeed is the snake venom powerful enough to kill an adult mongoose. The mongoose also has 28 (C)[dull / sharp] teeth, and it can bite with enough force to crack bones. It fights snakes by focusing on the head, often defeating them by smashing their skull.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) unafraid=두려워하지 않는 / afraid=두려워하는 (B) advantage=이점, 유리함 / weakness=약점 (C) sharp=날카로운 / dull=무딘
det.analysis:
① afraid—advantage—sharp: (A) 뱀을 사냥하는 몽구스라 '두려워하지 않는(unafraid)'이 맞음
② unafraid—advantage—sharp: 뱀을 '두려워하지 않고(unafraid)' + 날렵한 몸이 '이점(advantage)'을 주고 + '날카로운(sharp)' 이빨 ←정답
③ unafraid—weakness—dull: (B)(C) 날렵함은 '이점(advantage)'이고 이빨은 '날카로움(sharp)'
④ afraid—advantage—dull: (A)(C) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: unafraid(두려워하지 않는) 몽구스, advantage(이점), sharp(날카로운) 이빨

questions.passage: Since its discovery, researchers have found out that the circular shape might be due to slow-moving water currents __________ (flow) to one side of the island. But there is still no explanation for the lake's unusually cold, clear water.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: flow(흐르다) → flowing. 앞의 명사 currents를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사
det.analysis: flow를 현재분사 flowing으로 바꿔요. 'water currents __________ to one side'는 물살이 한쪽으로 '흐르는' 능동의 뜻이에요. 앞의 명사 currents(물살)를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사라서 flowing이 맞아요. (currents가 스스로 흐르는 능동이라 -ing형이에요.)
det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 꾸미며 능동(흐르는)의 뜻 → 현재분사 flowing

questions.passage: One of the most difficult conditions that patients deal with after a stroke is __________ (call) "hemispatial neglect." This condition occurs when the brain's parietal lobe is damaged.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: call(부르다) → called. be동사(is) 뒤에서 '~라고 불리다'라는 수동태를 만드는 과거분사
det.analysis: call을 과거분사 called로 변환. 'is called hemispatial neglect'는 '편측 공간 무시라고 불린다'라는 수동태예요. 「be동사(is) + 과거분사(called)」로 '~라고 불리다'라는 뜻을 만들어요.
det.tip: is __________ = 수동태(be + 과거분사) → call의 과거분사 called

questions.passage: It doesn't bother them when they are __________ (have) a conversation. But they feel uncomfortable when hearing a recording of it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: have(가지다) → having (be동사 뒤 현재진행형 -ing)
det.analysis: be동사(are) 뒤에서 '~하고 있는 중'이라는 진행의 뜻을 나타내려면 동사에 -ing를 붙여요. they are __________ a conversation은 '그들이 대화를 하고 있는 중'이라는 뜻이라 have를 having으로 바꿔야 해요.
det.tip: be동사(are) + 동사-ing = 진행형 → having

questions.passage: Blue wavelengths help us during the day by __________ (improve) our mood and increasing our attention span. However, they seem to be the most disruptive at night.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: improve(동사: 향상시키다) → improving (동명사). 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사가 오고, 뒤의 increasing과 병렬 구조
det.analysis: 동사 improve를 동명사 improving으로 바꿔요. 'by __________ our mood'에서 by는 전치사예요. 전치사 뒤에는 동사가 그대로 올 수 없고 동명사(-ing) 형태가 와야 해요. 게다가 바로 뒤에 나오는 increasing과 'by improving ~ and increasing ~'처럼 나란히(병렬) 이어지므로 형태도 똑같이 improving이 맞아요.
det.tip: 전치사 by + 동명사, 그리고 뒤의 increasing과 병렬 → improving

questions.passage: Brazil's Jungle Marathon, __________ (hold) in the Amazon rainforest every October, is one of the world's most challenging competitions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: hold(열다, 개최하다) → held(과거분사). 명사 뒤에서 '~에서 열리는'으로 수동으로 꾸미는 자리
det.analysis: hold를 과거분사 held로 바꿔요. 'Brazil's Jungle Marathon, __________ in the Amazon rainforest, is ~'에서 마라톤은 매년 '열리는' 대상이라 수동 관계예요. 그래서 콤마 사이의 분사구는 과거분사 held(열리는)로 앞 명사를 꾸며요.
det.tip: 행사가 '열리는' 수동 관계 → 과거분사 held (분사구 후치수식)
